Medical Imaging Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A Survey



Uma Sharma1, *, Deeksha Sharma1, Pooja Pathak2, Sanjay Kumar Singh2, Pushpanjali Singh3
1 Inderprastha Engineering College, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh 201009, India
2 ABES Engineering College, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh 201009, India
3 Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam University, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh 226031, India

Abstract

Machine learning and deep learning which are the subsets of Artificial intelligence, have numerous uses in medical imaging. Advancements in machine learning and deep learning led to drastic improvements in medical imaging fields like the evaluation of risks, recognition, identification, prediction, and treatment results. The decision-making power of computers based on artificial intelligence has elevated the effectiveness and efficiency of human decisions. Techniques based on machine learning and deep learning are not only effective and efficient but also speedy. In the medical field, the stage of the diagnosed disease is of great importance as the treatment and recovery rates depend on it. So based on the best and fastest decisions given by machine learning and deep learning techniques, medical practitioners can give their services in a better way.

We have given a summary of the methods used in medical imaging based on machine learning and deep learning algorithms with the benefits and pitfalls of these algorithms. These algorithms offer remarkable methods for classification, segmentation, and autonomous decision-making ability for the analysis of medical images.

Keywords: CNN, Deep learning, Medical image, Machine learning, RNN.

* Corresponding author Uma Sharma: Inderprastha Engineering College, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh 201009, India; E-mail: umasharma107@gmail.com

INTRODUCTION

In the field of medical imaging, significant impressions of the images give the idea about the overall health of an individual. But the main work is the study of these patterns. These impressions must be studied by a team of experts as only one view is not able to give the exact information. For best results, images are to

be analyzed repeatedly but still, this can give wrong results. Medical imaging has seen significant advancements with the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. These technologies have shown promise in various aspects of medical imaging, including boosting efficiency, helping with treatment planning, and increasing diagnostic accuracy. These techniques can best extract the image features for making the diagnosis of interest [1]. Many machine learning and deep learning techniques are available but artificial neural networks are the foundation of medical imaging [2-4]. Mathematical calculations are involved in artificial neural networks which imitate the function of the human brain.

The number of nodes decides the complexity and intelligence level of the decision or work done. CNN and RNN are the branches of neural networks also used in medical imaging. In CNN, after the starting layer, specific filter layers, activation layers, and pooling layers are used [5]. In the end, minute features are recognized by using different layers. In the RNN (Recurrent Neural Network), due to recurrent linkages of the nodes, previous flow patterns are stored or remembered by the network. In medical imaging, the release of information is scattered over multiple layers with the relation among different layers. So it is the beauty of RNN that the related information can be extracted from the previous layers to better understand the subsequent layers [6].

In the first part of the paper, we have discussed different medical imaging methods, then in the second part, machine learning techniques related to medical diagnosis are explained under the categories of supervised and unsupervised learning. In the next part, the role of deep learning in medical imaging is discussed. After that, open-source tools are given for the implementation of machine learning techniques. Finally, the conclusion is set out.

MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS

Medical Imaging

Maximum techniques involved in medical imaging are based on small incisions so that doctors can see inside the body without surgery. In the medical field, numerous imaging methods are there, which are helpful in the identification and cure of many medical disorders. Each method has its advantages and disadvantages (Fig. 1).

Fig. (1))
General medical imaging method.

X-Ray Imaging

X-rays are ionizing radiations that interact with electrons in orbits rather than the nuclei as their energy levels are low. It is called ionizing energy as it provides energy that is sufficient for the ionization of atoms. Its wavelength is from 0.01nm to 10 nm. Medical diagnosis through X-ray is a noninvasive technique as X-rays can pass through the body without any incision. The type of material is responsible for the amount of X-ray absorption and scattering inside the matter.

In the X-ray tube, the filament wire emits electrons, and these electrons are drawn toward the revolving anode, which produces the alternating current. The focus point on the anode generates X-rays. Based on a particular area or problem, the contrast of rays can be increased for better picture contrast. Photostimulable phosphor (PSP) plates are used as receptors in X-ray radiography [7]. After acquiring the digital image from PSP, the image is scaled and recorded. Fig. (2) shows the concept of an X-ray imaging system.

Fig. (2))
X-ray imaging system.

Ultrasound Imaging

Ultrasound methods of medical imaging are quite popular these days. These methods are affordable as compared to other medical imaging techniques. Ultrasound methods are safe for the health of humans and animals as compared to magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission tomography [8].

One disadvantage of ultrasound imaging is that it is affected by noise and has poor image quality as compared to other imaging techniques. Also, the expert operator is the main requirement of ultrasound imaging as the quality of the image depends upon the skill of the operator. Three-dimensional ultrasound images give better view and diagnosis as compared to two-dimensional images but 3D imaging is costlier than 2D imaging. So, research is going on converting 2D images into 3D images [9]. In ultrasound imaging, machine learning is used according to the organ or body location classification for breast, liver, spine, and eye images, segmentation is used for the heart, brain, and placenta, and regression is used for the fetal brain, prostate, etc.

Diagnostic systems should be smart enough to make decisions based on ultrasound imaging. As shown in Fig. (3), firstly the system should be trained for decision making and then the doctors can advise for immediate guidance [10].

Fig. (3))
Machine learning-based us system.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging

Machine Learning and deep learning will play a significant role in the study of magnetic resonance imaging in the upcoming years. With effective decision-making power, this system will provide better picture quality and reduced procuring time. It will also increase the speed of the work [11-13]. Increased speed is the solution to the problem of a limited number of scanners. Fig. (4) shows the basic components of a magnetic resonance imaging system. In magnetic resonance imaging, a variety of tasks can be done using machine learning techniques; for example image classification, segmentation, and regression. In classification and segmentation, local labels are given to the images. After sensing, the image formation is the reconstruction in MRI, which is done with the help of regression that assigns continuous predictions for every pixel value in the picture [14]. Image noise can also be reduced in MR imaging using machine learning. If the components of the forward model are not known, then the approximated function can be used.

Computerized Tomography

Computerized tomography (CT), commonly referred to as computed tomography or CT scan is a medical imaging procedure that produces comprehensive cross-sectional pictures of the body using X-ray technology. An X-ray machine with unique capabilities is used in the CT scan procedure, and it revolves around the patient. A computer processes the obtained data to produce intricate, two-dimensional pictures or three-dimensional reconstructions of the interior components.

Fig. (4))
Magnetic resonance imaging components.

Mammography

A specialist medical imaging method created especially for examining the breasts is called mammography. It is essential for the early identification and detection of breast cancer. Low-dose X-rays are used in mammograms to get finely detailed pictures of the breast tissue.

MACHINE LEARNING

Healthcare is of utmost importance among all industries where security and authenticity are the highest priority. With the widespread adoption of image acquisition and medical data, many countries are taking measures to safeguard electronic patient records. This is particularly crucial as medical images play a pivotal role in telesurgery and telediagnosis, facilitating physician training and enabling discussions among healthcare professionals based on past diseases and treatments. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) becomes essential in this context, contributing to the advancement of medical practices and enhancing the effectiveness of healthcare systems [15]. Machine Learning (ML) empowers doctors to make real-time decisions by leveraging extensive patient information and collective knowledge gained from experiences, moving beyond conventional programmed rules. Unlike traditional models based on predetermined equations, ML learns from inputs and outputs, adapting through training with the aid of optimization algorithms. This iterative process refines the models to provide accurate predictions for the given training data. The overarching goal of ML is to cultivate mathematical models capable of delivering beneficial outcomes when presented with new input data. ML finds diverse applications in the real world, including image processing, disease detection, natural language processing, speech recognition, and various other domains.

The healthcare system is experiencing a substantial surge in the demand for medical image services, encompassing various modalities such as radiography, endoscopy, mammography images (MG), nuclear medicine imaging, ultrasound images, magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), Positron Emission Tomography (PET), and pathological tests. Analyzing medical images poses a persistent challenge, compounded by the time-consuming nature of the process, often due to a shortage of radiologists. Machine Learning (ML) offers a promising solution by addressing these challenges, as it can learn and make predictions from data without requiring explicit programming, potentially enhancing the efficiency and accessibility of medical image analysis.

ML has three learning approaches, which are supervised learning, and unsupervised learning. Other learning approaches are reinforcement learning and recommender systems. The typical architecture of machine learning and deep learning is shown in Figs. (5 and 6). Supervision and training are the general concepts applied to both machine learning and deep learning.

Fig. (5))
Steps involved in machine learning with handcrafted medical images.
Fig. (6))
Workflow of Deep learning.

Machine Learning Techniques

Supervised Learning

Most of today's ML belongs to the supervised learning algorithm for medical applications. In this learning, models are based on known input and output data to predict future output. Supervised learning problems fall into two main categories: regression and classification. In regression, the goal is to predict outcomes with a continuous output or map input variables to a continuous function. In contrast, classification problems involve predicting outcomes with a discrete output, aiming to map input variables into distinct categories. For example, when dealing with a patient having a tumor, the objective is to predict whether the tumor is malignant or benign. This scenario exemplifies a classification-supervised learning task, where the focus is on categorizing input data into specific classes.

Numerous supervised ML algorithms are available in the literature, and each one has a unique method for predicting output values [16]. There are no ML algorithms that meet all the requirements of applications in the field of medicine. Therefore, finding the right ML algorithm is just based on experiments. There are few supervised machine learning algorithms such as support vector machine (SVM), decision trees, neural networks, nearest neighbor, naive Bayes, and linear regression, which are mostly used for the security and classification of medical images. In clinical terms, the input data is in the form of medical images or data and the output is in the form of prediction of disease, diagnosis of disease, and tells about the present condition of the patient.

In Support Vector Machines (SVM), data is classified by determining a hyperplane, which serves as the decision boundary, effectively separating input data from other classes with the maximum margin of separation. The linear function divides the input data, and a loss function is employed to identify instances where the data falls on the incorrect side of the hyperplane if a nonlinear function is used [8, 17]. SVM boasts several advantages, including its flexibility in hyperplane selection, strong capability, and a reduction in computational cost, which help mitigate overfitting issues. However, a significant drawback of SVM is its high computational time requirement for training datasets [18].

Unsupervised Learning

In unsupervised learning, we leave the computer to find labels, patterns, or structures in the given datasets. In this type of learning, we do not tell the algorithm in advance, we have only a bunch of data. A good illustration of unsupervised learning is clustering where the data lives in two different clusters. Clustering algorithms are used for a bunch of applications like organizing large computer clusters, social network analysis, market segmentation, object recognition, stock market data analysis, and also used for surprisingly astronomical data analysis [19].

A major obstacle in the field of medical imaging is the interpretation of images for the diagnosis and treatment of complicated diseases from high-dimensional and diverse data. Both types of algorithms, supervised and unsupervised deep learning have produced encouraging achievements in the field of medical image analysis in recent years. There are several published studies on supervised deep learning, but there are very few thorough evaluations on unsupervised deep learning for medical image analysis. So large scope of research is present in the field of unsupervised learning for medical image analysis. Different types of auto encoders, Deep Belief Networks, Deep Boltzmann Machines, and Generative Adversarial Networks are a few of the models that come under the umbrella of unsupervised learning for medical image analysis. Deep Belief Networks are feedforward neural networks with numerous hidden layers. DBNs are simple, unsupervised networks, such as restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) or autoencoders, where the visible layer of each sub-network is derived from its hidden layer.

The restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) is a type of generative stochastic artificial neural network capable of learning a probability distribution from its input data. RBMs find application in deep learning networks, where they contribute to the construction of deep belief networks. The process involves “stacking” RBMs and fine-tuning the resulting deep network is achieved through the use of gradient descent and backpropagation. This approach enables the creation of sophisticated and effective deep belief networks by leveraging the capabilities of RBMs.

There is also one more form of learning, semi-supervised learning that uses both supervised and unsupervised in which there is labeling of some parts of training data.

DEEP LEARNING

The application of the Deep Learning Approach (DLA) in medical image analysis is emerging as a rapidly expanding field of research. Deep learning, a specialized form of machine learning, involves the direct learning of application tasks from input data and has proven highly effective in the context of medical imaging. The design of deep learning often utilizes Neural Network (NN) algorithms. The term “deep” refers to the incorporation of numerous network levels. While traditional NNs typically consist of two or three layers, deep learning networks can encompass hundreds of layers. This approach finds diverse applications in the medical field, including medical data security, disease prediction, pattern recognition, and various other areas.

The primary difference between Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) is that both approaches concentrate on feature learning, more precisely, the automatic extraction of data representations. Supervised machine learning techniques include Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Unsupervised machine learning (ML) methods including Deep Belief Networks (DBNs), Boltzmann Machines, Autoencoders, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are often used in the field of medical picture analysis. CNNs are frequently used because of their efficacy for medical image processing tasks such as segmentation, classification, object recognition, and registration.

CNN (Convolution Neural Network)

The most widely utilized deep learning technique for medical applications is CNN, which is crucial for comprehending meaningful visual and structured data representations. Historically, before CNNs could be utilized efficiently, these qualities had to be manually designed or generated by less competent machine-learning models [20]. Many of the manually created picture characteristics were typically abandoned once it was possible to use feature detectors discovered by CNNs because they turned out to be nearly useless when compared to feature detectors learned directly from the data.

Basic Building Blocks of CNN

With extremely few connections between the layers, a CNN is a specific type of artificial neural network designed to preserve spatial correlations in the data. The input to a CNN is set up in a grid layout, and it is then passed through layers that maintain these connections, with each layer action using a little portion of the preceding layer. According to Fig. (7), a CNN uses Convolutional Layers, Rectified Linear Unit (RELU) Layers, and Pooling Layers to alter an input image made up of raw pixels. This feeds into a final Fully Connected Layer, which provides class scores or probabilities, classifying the input into the class with the greatest likelihood. So let us start with a brief description of the convolution layer.

Fig. (7))
Building blocks of CNN [25].

Convolutional Layer

Operating on two functions is known as a convolutional layer, where one function is of input values or image pixel values and the other function is filter or kernel. Both functions are presented as an array of two numbers and the multiplication of two functions gives an output. This process is continued till the whole image process is reached and that gives a feature named an activation map. Basically in an activation map or feature map, the kernel is highly active to see the features like dots or straight or curved lines in an image. Sparse connections, weights sharing, and equivariant representation are three key ML ideas that are used in convolution [21]. CNN has sparse connection means only a few input layers are connected to the next layer in contrast, a neural network includes all inputs, and each output neuron is coupled to a neuron. That gives important features to learn, which reduces the number of weights to be calculated and also greatly increases the efficiency of the algorithm.

Rectified Linear Unit (RELU) or Activation Layer

RELU is an activation function that only accepts positive values and lowers negative input values to zero. The RELU layer is a major aid in preventing the vanishing gradient problem by streamlining and optimizing training and computations. Sigmoid, tanh, leaky RELU, randomized RELU, and parametric RELUs are examples of frequent activation functions.

Pooling Layer

The pooling layer is positioned between the convolution layer and the RELU layer, serving to reduce the number of parameters to be computed as well as the height and width of the image. Various types of pooling exist, including max pooling, average pooling, and L2 normalization pooling, with max pooling being the most commonly employed. The primary role of max pooling is to select the highest input value within the kernel, discarding the remaining values. Essentially, it identifies the most dominant invariant feature within the pooling region.

Fully Connected Layer

In this, where every neuron in the previous layer is attached to every neuron in the last fully connected layer. Depending on the desired level of feature abstraction, there may be one or more fully connected layers in addition to convolution, pooling, and RELU. Essentially, this layer considers the set of powerful active features that would suggest the class to which the image belongs.

After Alex Net’s outstanding performance in 2012, CNNs have been employed more and more to improve the effectiveness of human physicians in processing medical images [22-24].

RNN (Recurrent Neural Network)

It is used to process sequential data or information and used for content analysis tasks such as machine translation, computer speech recognition, language modeling used in NLP (natural language processing), and text prediction [26, 27] because of their capability to produce text.

In a basic Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), the output of each layer is combined with the input of the next layer, providing a form of contextual “memory.” Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) have evolved from RNNs to address challenges related to the vanishing gradient problem during backpropagation through time. These are adjustments made to RNNs that allow them to hold long-term dependencies and ignore some of the collected information. For medical-related issues, RRN is used for image division.

Drawbacks of using deep learning for a clinical domain, and its prospects: Deep neural networks prove highly beneficial when making precise judgments based on intricate datasets. However, despite this significant advantage, employing deep learning methods comes with certain drawbacks. One primary limitation is the substantial requirement for both extensive training data and computational power. The process of training the model and obtaining accurate results is time-consuming due to these demands. A widely utilized deep learning technique is CNN, which necessitates labeled input for supervised learning. Manual labeling, particularly in case of medical images, poses a significant challenge. Addressing this challenge entails advancements in computational power, increased data storage, and continual enhancements in deep learning architectures. AI applications, specifically deep learning for medical image analysis, face the issue of unknown internal representations despite having well-defined inputs and outputs. Inherent problems such as noise and brightness issues in medical images are also prevalent. However, through preprocessing steps, the noise problem can be mitigated, contributing to ongoing improvements in performance levels over time [28].

MEDICAL IMAGING ANALYSIS WITH MACHINE LEARNING AND DEEP LEARNING

Medical image analysis's main goal is to locate the anatomically impacted areas of a disease, which helps doctors comprehend how lesions grow. Usually, this examination requires the following four crucial steps:

Image Preprocessing

The preprocessing stage eliminates undesirable distortions from images to improve the information inside the images.

Segmentation

This is the technique of separating particular areas, such as tumors or organs, for a more thorough examination of the image. It is essential for defining the region of interest (ROI) in the medical image data.

Feature Extraction

Feature extraction is the process of extracting specific information from ROIs. The process of feature extraction entails gathering pertinent data that aids in the identification and description of these ROIs.

Pattern Recognition or Classification

The last stage is classification, which entails grouping the ROIs based on the characteristics that were extracted. This stage facilitates the diagnostic procedure by helping to differentiate between various anatomical structure types or to spot anomalies.

The process begins with preprocessing to improve image quality, followed by segmentation to isolate regions of interest. Feature extraction focuses on capturing pertinent details from these regions, and classification utilizes the extracted features to categorize and identify the anatomical structures or abnormalities within the medical images. This systematic approach is crucial for providing valuable insights to healthcare professionals for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning [29].

Many image analysis techniques are there. Out of these, pixel-based analysis is commonly used. In pixel-based analysis, direct image pixels are taken into account instead of the extracted part of the image [30]. As several pixels in an image are very large, the time required to train the model is also very large in the case of machine learning with pixel-based analysis. Before applying this technique, the contrast of the image is enhanced using different filtering methods. For contrast enhancement, modification of histograms can also be made. Local binary patterns are used to apply machine learning to study medical images. It is used to give the spatial distribution of the edges of the image. A linear SVM classifier has been applied for good accuracy among all spatial edge descriptors [31, 32].

Neural networks are used in medical imaging to find the details of the disease. To classify cancerous cells and normal cells, neural networks are used. Neural network outcome for the classification of cells has great accuracy as compared to the previous voting methods of diagnosis [33]. Machine learning techniques may be used to develop a set of rules of clinical characters that specifically characterize the situation for the set of clinical problems to have intelligent systems. Information can therefore be expressed as a set of straightforward rules or, more frequently, as a decision tree. The channelized SVM is applied after CHO i.e. channelized hoteling observer, to improve the quality of an image.

Convolutional neural networks, CNN, which is part of deep learning, are popularly used for image analysis. In medical imaging, classification is an important part that tells about the clinical results of interest. CNN can be applied to the large variety and large volume of three-dimensional data. In the analysis of cervical cytopathology images, CNN is applied for image segmentation and image classification [34].

The registration process is used in medical pictures and data collected from various sensors. It is a procedure in which some basic parameters are identified as standards. Using deep learning techniques, a registration procedure is applied to find the degree of similarities between different images. Specifically, it is used in the field of medicine.

OPEN-SOURCE TOOLS

To support several stages of the machine learning workflow, including data pre-processing, model development, evaluation, and deployment, various open-source machine learning tools are available. To implement healthcare applications, there are some popular machine learning tools like TensorFlow, Keras, Octave, PyTorch, OpenCV, sci-kit-learn, OpenAI Gym, SimpleITK, and many more. For medical image analysis, libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy are commonly used [35].

TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Google. It is commonly used in medical imaging applications due to its flexibility, scalability, and extensive toolset for building and deploying machine learning models. Machine learning for medical imaging involves processes like data pre-processing, including image loading, resizing, normalization, and augmentation. The tools required for these processes are also available in Tensorflow. Pre-processing techniques are mainly provided by Tensorflow to prepare this data for model training. The training of different machine learning models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) used in medical imaging tasks can also be done by Tensorflow. CNN architectures are helpful to perform tasks like image classification, segmentation, object detection, and more. Through transfer learning, models trained on generic data can have their knowledge leveraged and customised to smaller datasets for particular medical imaging applications. TensorFlow can support medical image formats (DICOM, NIfTI, etc.) and carry out specialised tasks like image registration, analysis, or segmentation by integrating with medical imaging libraries such as SimpleITK, PyDICOM, or other domain-specific tools.

Keras is a high-level API for neural network construction that runs on top of TensorFlow and other frameworks. Deep neural networks can be built, trained, and deployed using Keras as it is a user-friendly interface. Keras can be used for a variety of tasks while dealing with medical imaging, including object detection, picture creation, segmentation, and image classification. It can also be used to obtain a dataset of medical images like X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs by providing annotations with required labels. The pre-processing of data can also be done on Keras by resizing, normalizing, augmenting, or carrying out additional required changes. Along with image classification architectures like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) such as VGG, ResNet, or custom architectures, Keras also utilised architectures for segmentation like U-Net. When working with medical imaging, Keras can employ various tasks like building, training, evaluating, and predicting the model [36].

There are some popular machine-learning libraries used in medical imaging. PyTorch is one of them as it is a popular open-source machine learning library, and has been extensively used in various healthcare applications due to its flexibility, efficiency, and robustness in developing deep learning models. PyTorch is developed by Facebook's AI Research lab. PyTorch has been used for tasks like reconstruction, classification, and segmentation of medical images. To diagnose diseases, segment tumours, and locate organs in medical pictures like MRIs, CT scans, and X-rays, deep learning models developed with PyTorch have been applied. Predictive models for diseases like cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases can be developed using PyTorch. The outcomes of these models are determined with patient data such as electronic health records (EHRs), lab reports, medical images, progression, or patients’ physical health. One other application of PyTorch is developing models for wearable devices like smartwatches and fitness trackers [37, 38].

CONCLUSION

The existing pool of medical information proves inadequate for making clinical decisions. This paper provides a concise introduction to medical images and explores the utilization of machine learning and deep learning in their analysis. Fundamentals of both supervised and unsupervised algorithms are covered. The survey reveals that CNN algorithms, having demonstrated favorable outcomes, are prevalently employed in medical image analysis. Nevertheless, there persist several challenges in medical image processing that necessitate attention. Deep learning algorithms emerge as potent tools, particularly beneficial for the upcoming generation of radiologists with limited experience. Their efficiency is also noteworthy in accurately predicting diseases within shorter time frames.

Applications of Machine Learning Practices in Human Healthcare Management Systems

Abstract

In the modern era, medical institutions offer patients high-quality, reasonably priced treatment, but they require sophisticated technology. But even with significant advancements in the computerization and digitalization of medicine, effective and reliable management solutions are still lacking. Medical operations are very complex, so high-level management is required. Machine learning techniques might be very useful in resolving these issues since they are scalable and adaptable to complex patterns. This study suggests that machine learning could improve human comprehension and oversight of healthcare operations, leading to more efficient healthcare delivery. The goal of the current study is to examine how machine learning methods can be used to detect diseases, various clinical trials, drug development, robotics-based surgery, organ image processing, and various challenges of machine learning in the medical industry. Finally, along with challenges, the study concludes that machine learning practices become essential for healthcare organizations of the modern era.

Keywords: Clinical trial, Drug development, Health care, Machine learning, Organs image processing, Treatment.

INTRODUCTION

“Machine Learning” (ML) is the branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI) that studies how to replicate human learning processes and improve their accuracy over time utilizing data and algorithms. ML includes various statistical techniques through

which computers learn from domain-related dataset.The present study explores the role of ML in the healthcare industry. Healthcare is a well-known domain that is benefitted from various ML techniques [1-3]. The human lifetime is enhanced through the advancement of medical facilities that are supported by an advanced healthcare system equipped with tools based on ML techniques.

These days, case studies of different diseases are being researched, and Big Data methods are being used to retain electronic records of these cases.

The electronic records include real-time information on clinical trials, which include patients’ visits to doctors, disease symptoms records, patients’ medical test information, and further prescription. In order to find and correct any possible prescription mistakes, Artificial Intelligence (AI) can thus examine the patient's medical records in addition to prescribed drugs. These electronic records become helpful for decision-making of patients’ diseases [4-6].

The clinical results of predictive analysis have saved time and cost of medical tests through which every individual patient gets suitable therapies and benefits [7-9].

Healthcare Machine Learning Foundations need high-quality and diverse datasets as these are crucial for training accurate ML models. The ML applications must adhere to strict ethical guidelines to ensure patient privacy and data security. ML ought to provide explanations for their predictions to gain trust of healthcare professionals and facilitate decision-making. The organizational and administrative aspects of providing healthcare, such as scheduling appointments in bed, supervising from a distance, and handling other tasks like creating the roster, greatly benefit from this technology.

Healthcare professionals spend time on redundant tasks such as maintaining and managing records and claims handling, which prevents them from offering the required medical care. Because machine learning has various features and applications, it has grown more and more important in the healthcare industry [10].

ML algorithms are capable of accurately predicting the course of a disease, the results of treatment, and the fate of the patient by analyzing vast volumes of patient data. ML can find patterns in medical pictures, such as MRIs and X-rays to help in the detection of illnesses like cancer [11]. Natural Language Processing enhances clinical decision-making, ML approaches may extract important information from unstructured medical data, such as patient records and doctor's notes.

ML algorithms can analyze vast amounts of molecular data to identify potential drug candidates and optimize drug development processes. This helps tailor treatment plans to individual patients based on their unique characteristics, improving treatment efficacy and minimizing adverse effects [12]. ML can assist in the early detection and accurate diagnosis of diseases, as well as predicting disease progression and patient outcomes. ML algorithms have been applied to discover patterns of abnormal skin, tumour domain areas, bleeding areas, etc.To identify and fix any pharmaceutical errors, AI can evaluate the prescription drugs and the patient's medical history. Optimizing hospital operations, resource allocation, and patient flow can result in cost savings and increased efficiency. All things considered, machine learning has the power to completely transform the healthcare industry by enhancing operational effectiveness, treatment results, and diagnosis. When everything is said and done, machine learning can dramatically change the healthcare sector by improving diagnosis, treatment outcomes, and operational effectiveness. The primary goal of the current study is to investigate machine learning's important role in the healthcare sector.

RESEARCH OBJECTIVES

High performance computing is quick and able to manage big, complicated data silos is produced, as modern technology becomes more and more popular in the healthcare industry.

Healthcare facilities are made possible by automated machine learning. Healthcare workers can now make full use of real-time data harvesting, innovative techniques, and effective programming interfaces offered by ML technology.

The major research objectives of the present study are:

a) To study the need for ML in the Healthcare Industry.

b) To explore various challenges of ML in the medical Industry.

c) To explore the role of ML applications in healthcare’s subareas: Medical.

NEED FOR MACHINE LEARNING IN THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY

The important reasons for machine learning in healthcare are disease predictive analytics, disease identification and diagnosis, personalized treatment plans, drug discovery and development, health monitoring and wearables, operational efficiency, fraud detection and security, remote patient monitoring, and population health management. In literature, the above factors are discussed at the micro level. Both the standard of medical care and the capacity to manage complicated illnesses are continuously improving. There are still numerous unanswered questions, nevertheless, particularly about the length and dosage of treatments depending on a patient's unique traits or for patient populations with limited clinical research, including children [13].

To forecast the most effective and customized therapies for kids, machine learning has been effectively incorporated into pediatric care in recent years. Since the COVID-19 pandemic began, machine learning has gained significant attention. Organizations have turned to machine learning (ML) to stay competitive and gain an edge, from streamlining operations to expanding R&D in an often tumultuous and unpredictable work environment. ML has aided healthcare systems and institutions in overcoming certain difficulties [14, 15].

One of the most intriguing advancements in AI is machine learning, which is being tried by many companies. A growing number of people are using ML. It applies to both commercial and healthcare settings and leverages algorithms to support data-driven learning. New ideas and technologies are always emerging, which means that healthcare is always evolving. In certain of these novel situations, machine learning could help doctors. Technological advancements and unstructured text can now yield insights that were previously difficult to produce and distribute widely. Administrators and physicians may make timely, well-informed choices about patient care and operational initiatives that have an international effect by using this increased depth of ML-derived knowledge [16-18].

CHALLENGES OF MACHINE LEARNING IN THE MEDICAL INDUSTRY

Experts must investigate and debate several issues that crop up when using ML algorithms in the healthcare industry. The following are a few of the numerous obstacles to machine learning implementation in the medical field:

Data Availability and Quality

It might be difficult to get varied and high-quality medical data for machine learning model training. Medical data is challenging to gather and standardize as it is frequently complicated, unstructured, and dispersed across many sources [19].

Data Security and Privacy

Sensitive medical data is governed by stringent privacy laws. Using machine learning algorithms to ensure data privacy and security is a serious problem since it calls for strong security measures to safeguard patient data [20].

Interpretability and Transparency

The machine learning models frequently function as “black boxes,” and it can be difficult to understand how decisions are made. Interpretability is essential in medical apps to win over healthcare professionals' confidence and make sure the judgments made by the models make sense [21].

Limited Sample Sizes

Medical datasets, particularly those about uncommon diseases or particular patient populations, are sometimes of a limited size. Machine learning models' performance may be impacted by sparse data [22].

Regulatory Compliance

Because the medical field is so tightly regulated, applying machine learning algorithms has to abide by stringent laws like the US's HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act). It might be difficult to follow these rules while creating and implementing machine learning models.

Integration into Healthcare Systems

Compatibility problems, interoperability challenges, and reluctance to change from healthcare experts can make it difficult to integrate machine learning technology into the current healthcare systems [23].

Bias and Fairness

When machine learning models are trained on data that contains prejudices, they may unintentionally reinforce those biases, which might result in discriminatory or unjust outcomes when making medical decisions. The most important tasks in ML are addressing bias and guaranteeing fairness.

Clinical Adoption and Validation

Before machine learning algorithms are widely used in medicine, it is crucial to validate their effectiveness and clinical value. It might take a lot of time and resources to carry out thorough clinical trials and prove these algorithms' efficacy and safety.

It is crucial to remember that machine learning in the medical profession is still developing and that these difficulties are not all-inclusive. To fully utilize machine learning in enhancing healthcare outcomes, researchers and practitioners are proactively tackling these obstacles.

APPLICATIONS OF MACHINE LEARNING IN HEALTHCARE

In present research, some applications of ML in healthcare are described as:

Machine Learning in Medical Diagnosis

In the modern era, the ML models play an essential role in the healthcare industry diagnosis. Conventional diagnosis procedures are expensive, time-consuming, and frequently call for human involvement. Traditional diagnosis procedures are limited by an individual's abilities, but machine learning (ML)-based systems are not constrained by this, and unlike humans, robots do not experience fatigue. This could lead to the development of a technique for diagnosing diseases when there are unexpectedly more patients than needed in the medical system. Healthcare data, such as pictures (X-ray, MRI) and tabular data (patient conditions, age, and gender), are used to construct machine-learning-based disease diagnosis systems [24].

Machine Learning algorithm uses Decision trees, K-nearest neighbor, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes and AdaBoost algorithms in decision making of medical diagnosis. The Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models play a vital role in pathology, oncology, and genetic disorder patient’s image detection [25]. Fig. (1). illustrates the diseases diagnosed by Machine Learning Techniques [26].

Fig. (1))
Diseases diagnosed by machine learning techniques.

The important microscopy work that pathologists have historically performed can be improved by computer vision and machine learning. Diagnostic apps that assess physiological data, environmental variables, and hereditary factors frequently use machine vision. Modern machine learning techniques are used by medical personnel in triage to identify anomalies and give priority to patients who pose a threat to life. In a similar vein, AI helps doctors diagnose heart arrhythmias, forecast the prognosis of strokes, and manage chronic illnesses. Ansari et al. (2011) presented an automated technique based on neuro-fuzzy integrated systems for identifying coronary heart disease that produced an accuracy of almost 89% [27]. Rubin et al. (2017) employed deep convolution neural network-based methods to detect irregular heart sounds. The sensitivity and specificity of the training dataset were enhanced by the authors' modification of the loss function [28]. Nephropathy or injury to the kidneys is referred to as renal disease, or kidney disease commonly. Patients may have declining kidney function, if kidney sickness is not treated right that can lead to renal failure. Ma et al. (2020) identified chronic renal disease by using a collection of datasets containing data from various sources. The accuracy ranged from 87-90% with their suggested heterogeneous modified artificial neural network [29]. Breast cancer diagnoses have been made with success using machine learning approaches. Several medical professionals have proposed that early diagnosis of breast cancer may be possible using ML-based analysis. For example, Miranda and Felipe (2015) suggested computer-aided detection systems for breast cancer classification based on fuzzy logic [30]. The ML techniques have been successfully applied in the diagnoses of diabetes, its types and the identification of diabetic retinopathy. Ali et al. (2020) have used a KNN-based model for diabetes classification with 4900 samples [31]. Tsao et al. (2018) have developed ANN models to predict diabetic retinopathy with an accuracy of 79.5% [32]. The COVID-19 pandemic has emerged as humanity's most historical challenge. Li et al. (2020) developed the COVNet model with 96% accuracy using a large dataset of 4356 chest CT scans of pneumonia patients, 1296 of which were confirmed COVID-19 cases [33]. Hemdan et al. (2020) accurately identified COVID-19 patients from chest X-ray images with an accuracy of 90% and 95% using the VGG19 and ResNet50 models, utilizing a short dataset of just 50 images, respectively [34].

Machine Learning in Clinical Trail

Machine learning (ML) is increasingly being utilized in various aspects of clinical trials to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and improve decision-making processes. Here are several ways in which ML is applied in clinical trials:

Patient Enrolment and Eligibility Requirements

Machine learning algorithms examine using extra patient data and electronic health records (EHRs) to identify potential clinical trial participants. By forecasting patient outcomes and taking into account a wider range of patient variables, machine learning aids in the improvement of eligibility criteria.

Trial Protocol Design and Optimization

ML can help with adaptive clinical trial design, which modifies the trial design in response to interim data. The most productive and economical trial design can be found using optimization methods.

Endpoint Prediction and Biomarker Identification

Machine learning (ML) can be used to find potential biomarkers for diseases and predict patient outcomes. This can help pick meaningful endpoints for clinical trials. Finding patient subgroups that might react differentially to therapies is made easier with the help of predictive modelling.

Data Monitoring and Quality Assurance

Real-time monitoring and analysis of clinical trial data using machine learning algorithms can spot possible anomalies or problems with data quality. Trial results can be made more accurate and reliable with the help of automated data-cleaning procedures.

Drug Development and Discovery

Biological data is analyzed, prospective drug targets are found, and the effectiveness of therapeutic candidates is predicted through the application of machine learning (ML). Drug candidates can be ranked in the order of importance for future research using predictive modelling.

Predicting and Tracking Adverse Events

By examining patient data, machine learning algorithms are able to anticipate and track adverse events, which can assist researchers and clinicians in taking proactive steps to control risks. Information can be extracted from reports and clinical notes using natural language processing (NLP).

Real-world Evidence (RWE) Generation

Beyond the controlled setting of clinical trials, machine learning can analyse real-world data to produce supplementary evidence.

In addition to standard clinical trial data, RWE can offer insights into therapy efficacy and safety in patient populations encountered in the real world.

Even though machine learning (ML) has a lot of potential for improving clinical trials, there are a few issues that must be resolved before ML can be successfully incorporated into the process. These problems include the need for high-quality data, regulatory considerations, and the interpretability of machine learning algorithms.

Machine Learning in Drug Development

Machine learning assists in the identification of novel drug candidates by analyzing large datasets, predicting molecular interactions, and speeding up the discovery process.

Target Identification

ML models analyse biological data to discover possible therapeutic targets, making it easier to choose proteins or genes that are important for disease intervention.

Predicting Drug-Drug Interactions

During development, machine learning helps to reduce side effects and increase safety profiles by assisting in the prediction of likely drug interactions.

In bioinformatics, ML is applied to evaluate genomic and proteomic data, uncovering patterns that help with illness comprehension and therapy target prioritization.

Machine Learning Models Help with Drug Formulation Optimization

By forecasting the interactions between various substances, machine learning models help with drug formulation optimization by improving medicine delivery and bioavailability.

Clinical Trial Optimization

By analyzing patient data, machine learning algorithms optimize protocol adjustments, patient selection, and clinical trial design, leading to shorter trial durations and reduced costs.

Drug Efficacy Prediction

Machine learning algorithms are capable of evaluating patient data to forecast a drug's effectiveness in certain demography, supporting individualized medicine and treatment strategies. To help with patient classification and customized treatment options, machine learning finds significant biomarkers associated with illnesses.

Drug Repurposing

Machine Learning algorithms can be used to analyze existing drug data to identify potential new uses, which will speed up the creation of medications for other ailments.

Toxicity Prediction

By using machine learning to forecast the likely toxicity of potential treatments, compounds can be removed sooner. Drug dosage and delivery can be optimized because machine learning algorithms predict drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).

Genomic Medicine

By using genomic data to modify drug regimens based on a patient's genetic composition, ML increases the effectiveness of treatment.

Patient Stratification

Machine learning (ML) examines patient data to identify subsets that similarly react to treatment, enabling the development of customized medications and lowering trial variability.

Utilization of Real-World Information

Machine learning processes real-world patient data to provide information on medication efficacy and safety outside of controlled clinical trials.

Data Integration

To give a full knowledge of illness causes and medication responses, ML combines heterogeneous datasets such as genetic, clinical, and omics data. ML improves medication manufacturing processes by anticipating ideal conditions, lowering production costs, and maintaining consistent quality.

Market Access and Commercialization

Machine learning (ML) aids market access tactics by analysing market patterns, identifying patient demographics, and forecasting commercial success for a novel treatment.

Machine learning offers continuous learning from fresh data, allowing drug developers to adjust methods and enhance decision-making throughout the drug development lifecycle.

Robotic-based Surgery

In the realm of robotic-based surgery, machine learning has become a potent instrument that is transforming the way surgeries are carried out. Concerning ML in self-driving robotic surgery, one may think about letting the robot carry out these surgical gestures autonomously. The surgical job has a comprehensive and current understanding that is readily available when a robotic system demonstrates time that can accurately display an acceptable degree of competence in carrying out the relevant surgical actions to comparable surgical situations. A variation in this machine learning-based approach may be used in robotics-based surgery:

Surgeons can receive assistance in planning intricate robotic procedures from machine learning algorithms that analyze patient data, including electronic health records and medical imaging. This enhances patient outcomes and optimizes the surgical strategy [35]. During robotic operations, machine learning algorithms may offer real-time feedback and decision help. These algorithms can assist surgeons in making deft judgments at crucial times by evaluating data from surgical equipment and patient vitals. Through robotic operations, medical images may be analyzed to identify structures of interest using machine learning techniques like computer vision. This facilitates accurate tool navigation and targeting during surgery. Surgeons using robotic surgical systems may identify and interpret their hand gestures and motions using machine learning techniques. This improves surgical dexterity and allows intuitive control [36]. Machine learning algorithms can assess a surgeon's competence level by looking at surgical performance data [37]. This can assist in pinpointing areas in need of development and provide tailored training suggestions.

To predict surgical outcomes and potential issues, machine learning algorithms may analyze historical surgical data. This helps doctors conducting robotic surgery to minimize risks and make well-informed judgments.

Robotic surgical systems that use machine learning algorithms may learn from previous surgeries and modify their behavior accordingly [38]. This opens the door to minimally invasive robotic procedures that operate on their own. Using machine learning techniques, researchers may find patterns, trends, and insights by analysing vast amounts of surgical data. This expedites research in medicine and makes evidence-based advancements in robotic surgery possible.

Machine Learning in Organ Image Processing

Healthcare organ image processing is greatly aided by machine learning. Among the modalities of digital medical images may include X-rays, Ultrasound, computed tomography, magnetic-resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, retinal photographs, histology slides, and dermoscopy images. Some modalities—like Computed Tomography and Magnetic Resonance Images—examine many organs, while others—like dermoscopy and retinal photography—are organ-specific. Additionally, the quantity of data produced by every study differs. A single MRI scan can take up several hundred gigabytes, but a histology slide is only a few megabytes in size. This has technical ramifications for the pre-processing of the data and the architecture of an algorithm in terms of CPU and memory [39]. In organ image processing, machine learning is useful in the following ways:

Through analysing organ pictures, machine learning algorithms can aid with automated illness or abnormality detection, enabling medical practitioners to make fast and correct judgment. By lowering noise, increasing contrast, and boosting resolution, machine learning algorithms can improve the quality of organ pictures, facilitating improved interpretation and visualization. Precise organ segmentation from medical pictures is possible through machine learning techniques, which enable exact measurements and analysis. This facilitates the planning of operations, evaluation of tumour development, and tracking of therapeutic outcomes. Computer learning models may be trained to identify certain illnesses or ailments in pictures of organs, including tumours, lesions, or anomalies. This may help with treatment planning and early discovery. Organ pictures, medical records, genetic data, and other vast volumes of patient data may all be analysed by machine learning to find trends and create individualized treatment regimens [40]. Overall, better patient outcomes, more precise and quick diagnosis, and enhanced treatment planning are made possible by machine learning in organ image processing.

RISK MANAGEMENT IN HEALTHCARE THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING

The healthcare industry may find that machine learning (ML) has a big impact on risk management. There are some methods that machine learning can be used to improve risk management in the healthcare industry:

Finding and Preventing Fraud

Fraud in medical billing and insurance claims can be identified with machine learning models. It is possible to mark abnormalities and unusual trends in billing data for additional research. In addition to ensuring that funds are given to actual healthcare needs, this helps reduce financial losses brought on by fraudulent claims.

Medical Decision Assistance Frameworks

Healthcare practitioners can make better decisions by integrating machine learning (ML) into clinical decision support systems. Personalized treatment suggestions can be generated by machine learning models through patient data analysis, which lowers errors and raises overall care quality.

Risk Management for Security and Privacy

By detecting and reducing security threats in healthcare IT systems, machine learning (ML) can help shield patient data from hacking and unwanted access. Unusual patterns that can point to a security risk can be found via anomaly detection algorithms, enabling quick response.

Patient Involvement and Tracking: Healthcare providers can monitor and interact with patients remotely in real-time by using machine learning (ML). Proactive actions that reduce the likelihood of problems and hospital readmissions can result from early recognition of changes in patient circumstances.

Monitoring Adverse Drug Events

To detect possible side effects of medications, machine learning algorithms can examine electronic health records and other sources of healthcare data. This aids in the early identification of drug-related hazards, enabling medical professionals to take the necessary steps, such as changing a patient's prescription or closely monitoring them.

FUTURE SCOPE OF MACHINE LEARNING IN THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY

Machine Learning (ML) has a great deal of potential applications in the healthcare sector. This is possible to revolutionize various aspects of healthcare delivery, patient outcomes, and operational efficiency. Here are some significant areas where ML is expected to play a crucial role in the future of healthcare:

Personalized Medicine

To estimate a patient's risk of contracting a disease and suggest a customized course of therapy, ML will evaluate their genetics, medical history, and lifestyle data. Healthcare will become more effective and efficient as a result of this.

Better Diagnostics

Large volumes of medical data can be used to train ML algorithms to find trends and abnormalities, which can result in earlier and more precise diagnoses. This will be especially beneficial for complicated illnesses like cancer.

Drug Discovery and Development

The application of machine learning (ML) in drug discovery and development can expedite and reduce the cost of drug development by identifying new therapeutic targets and streamlining the process.

Robotics and Surgery

Because ML-powered robots offer more precision and less invasive operations; they are being employed in surgery. As a result, patients will heal more quickly and have better results.

Mental Health

Persons at risk of mental health issues can be identified by using ML to examine patient data. Better outcomes may result from using this to offer early intervention and assistance.

Public Health

ML can track the spread of illnesses and forecast outbreaks by analyzing big datasets. This will support public health officials in preventing pandemics by taking preventative action.

Administrative Efficient

Machine learning can automate numerous administrative duties in the healthcare industry, including the processing of insurance claims and appointment scheduling. This will allow medical professionals to spend more time with patients.

Research and Development

Machine learning (ML) can be used to evaluate vast volumes of research data to find new areas of study and hasten the creation of novel therapies.

Worldwide Health

Applying machine learning (ML) to underprivileged people can help reduce the cost of healthcare. Global health results will be enhanced by this.

CONCLUSIONS

The multidisciplinary field of machine learning encompasses several academic fields, including probability theory, statistics, and algorithm-based complexity theory. It focuses on the ways that computers mimic or actualize human learning patterns to pick up new information or abilities and rearrange already-existing knowledge structures to keep getting better at what they do. The following conclusions can be made from the tests presented in this article. The machine learning-based image recognition system helps in the categorization of different diseases by analysing and summarizing patient medical records. It can lessen the workload for medical workers while also increasing their productivity. Simultaneously, machine learning-based picture recognition technology is capable of detecting hidden disorders that are challenging for physicians to identify in children during their formative years and better safeguarding their development. This technique can assist the pharmaceutical industry in producing higher-quality medications that function more quickly and have fewer negative effects than traditional medications.

Any physician, scientist, or researcher can use machine learning (ML) as a valuable tool. It feels like machine learning is making progress every day. The medical sector is closely monitoring the ongoing advancements in machine learning (ML). Medical professionals and surgeons are using machine learning (ML) ideas to help save lives, identify illnesses and issues before they arise, improve patient care, include patients more effectively in their recuperation, and much more. Global organizations use machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance healthcare delivery. Organizations and pharmaceutical companies can create cures for serious illnesses more quickly and efficiently with the use of this technology. Virtual clinical trials, sequencing, and pattern recognition can now help businesses expedite their observation and testing procedures [41]. The most reliable indicators of general health include health behaviors and socioeconomic characteristics including education, social support systems, and income. Health organizations understand that to promote total health, they must target the full individual, including lifestyle and environment. Patients who are more likely to develop chronic diseases like diabetes, heart disease, or other avoidable conditions can be identified by ML models.
